title: FeatureSpec
description: Structured spec of a paper's design feature, emitted by the distiller node. Downstream integration agents implement against this document, so it must be complete enough to implement without the paper.

source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables

summary: The sr component exploits correlations between register values and branch directions by generating short digests of newly produced logical register values. It feeds these digests into the Statistical Corrector (SC). The feature is particularly effective immediately after a branch misprediction, as many in-flight instructions have finished and updated their registers by the time the predictor restarts, providing rich context to correct subsequent mispredictions.

state.name: register_tracking_table
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits), decay_ctr (8 bits)

state.name: sr_usefulness_table
state.organization: 8 banks, 8 entries per bank. Each entry stores a usefulness weight vector for the 8 or 9 logical registers assigned to that bank.

state.name: sr_prediction_table
state.organization: 8 banks of prediction counters. INFERRED: 8192 total entries across banks to match the 53863 total bit budget.
state.indexing: Hash of PC and register digest

algorithms.name: allocate_destination
algorithms.pseudocode:
R = dest_logical_reg
Table[R].payload = ROB_index
Table[R].valid = 0
Table[R].decay_ctr = 0
algorithms.notes: Reserves the register entry for the in-flight instruction. All entries also increment their decay_ctr on every decode; if decay_ctr >= 256, valid is cleared.

algorithms.name: update_digest
algorithms.notes: Generates a 12-bit digest. Assumed: 3 bits for leading, 3 for trailing counts for INT based on 6 remaining bits.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
sR_sum = 0
for bank in 0 to 7:
  UT_entry = UT[bank][skew(PC)]
  best_reg = max_useful_valid_reg(UT_entry, Table, bank)
  if best_reg:
    idx = hash(PC, Table[best_reg].payload)
    sR_sum += WT[bank][idx]
return sR_sum
algorithms.notes: Selects the digest of the most useful available register in each bank, bypassing a need for extra memory ports.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.pseudocode:
for bank in 0 to 7:
  avail_regs = get_valid_regs_at_prediction(Table, bank)
  if empty(avail_regs): continue
  chosen_reg = random_choice(avail_regs)
  UT_entry = UT[bank][skew(PC)]
  update_counter(UT_entry[chosen_reg], usefulness)
  idx = hash(PC, Table[chosen_reg].payload)
  update_counter(WT[bank][idx], branch_outcome)
algorithms.notes: Updates correlation for only one randomly selected available register per bank.

host_interfaces.need: Logical destination register ID at decode
host_interfaces.description: Used to track the producer and invalidate the previous digest of the register being overwritten.
host_interfaces.fallback: Invalidate the digest at rename or dispatch.

host_interfaces.need: Result value, register ID, and type at completion
host_interfaces.description: Used to compute the new digest as soon as the value is available in the execution unit.
host_interfaces.fallback: Compute and update the digest at commit (may cause stale digests for immediate dependent branches).

host_interfaces.description: Used to increment the decay counter to age and invalidate stale digests after 256 decoded instructions.
host_interfaces.fallback: Use instruction fetch or commit events as a proxy for age.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Register Tracking Table: 1495 bits; sR UT: 3216 bits (INFERRED from 6 * (65 * 8 + 8 + 8)); sR WT: 49152 bits (INFERRED to match total budget, implies 8192 entries).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires logic to compute 12-bit digests (e.g., leading/trailing zero/one counters), a 65-entry tracking table, 8 parallel max-reductions for usefulness, and random selection logic for training.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: Base bimodal table or other SC components (e.g., local histories) can be shrunk to pay for this feature.

parameters.name: decay_interval
parameters.storage_impact: Log2 of interval sets the decay_ctr width in the Register Tracking Table.

parameters.name: digest_width
parameters.storage_impact: Changes the payload width in the Register Tracking Table.

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Linearly scales the number of UT and WT tables, significantly impacting total sR storage.

unit_tests.name: Digest Decay
unit_tests.given: Register R1 is updated. 256 instructions are decoded. A branch is predicted.
unit_tests.expect: R1's valid bit is cleared; its digest is not used for prediction.

unit_tests.name: INT Digest Formatting
unit_tests.expect: The generated digest reflects the count of leading zeros, trailing zeros, and the least significant bits (0x0F).

unit_tests.name: Random Update Selection
unit_tests.given: Registers R2 and R3 in the same bank are both valid at prediction. The branch resolves.
unit_tests.expect: The predictor updates the UT and WT for exactly one randomly selected register.

open_questions: What are the exact bit widths of the leading/trailing zero/one counts in the INT digest? Assumed: 3 bits each, to leave 6 bits for the LSBs and total 12 bits.
How does the leading/trailing logic decide between counting zeros or ones? Assumed: count zeros if positive, ones if negative (sign extension).

The paper specifies sR WT size as '6x 2^7 + 2^8 + 2^9 x 8', which evaluates to 26880 bits, but the total sR storage is 53863 bits. Assumed: WT actually contains 8192 entries (49152 bits) to make the math work.
What hash functions and PC-skewing functions are used to index the UT and WT?
